brief_favorable_conditions: Shaded rocky streams (15–20 °C), permanent year-round flow, intact pathogen-free rainforest.
why_these_variables: Temperature plus dry-season rain and soil water, which together indicate whether streams keep flowing all year.

variables.label: Mean air temperature
variables.aggregation: Day-weighted annual mean of monthly means

variables.label: Dry-season rainfall
variables.aggregation: Rainfall summed over the location's 4 driest months (1981–2025 average cycle)

t2m_mean.model_description: Least-squares straight line through the training years
t2m_mean.summary_text: Mean air temperature in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 20.1 °C (80% range for 2030: 19.1–21.0 °C), above the 1991–2020 average of 19.4 °C (+0.70 °C).

precip_dry_season.model_description: Average of the last 10 training years (assumes recent conditions persist)
precip_dry_season.data_caution: Reanalysis rainfall is the least reliable NASA POWER variable. Several sites show large multi-year shifts (e.g. Bramble Cay 2015–2025 about 42 % drier than 1981–2014; Monteverde dry-season rain about 3 times higher in 2009–2025 than in 1981–2008). A change-point test places these shifts in different years (1998–2015), so they do not point to a single data-source switch, but they may still be partly artificial. Rainfall forecasts that extend such shifts are uncertain: show the 80 % range and verify against local rain gauges before presenting them as fact.
precip_dry_season.summary_text: Dry-season rainfall in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 129.6 mm (80% range for 2030: 10.1–229.7 mm), below the 1991–2020 average of 181.4 mm (-51.9 mm).
